programme: GATA3, RORC, and HLX are the canonical lineage-specifying master transcription factors for Th2, Th17, and Th1 CD4+ T cell fates respectively; MSC (musculin), a bHLH repressor of the Th2 cytokine locus whose targets here include FOXP3, CTLA4 and IL10, tips the balance away from GATA3's programme and toward a Treg/Th1-leaning state; TCF12, an E-protein (HEB) whose targets (CD4, PTCRA, TAL1) mark early thymocyte lineage commitment, sits upstream of all of them as the developmental scaffold that licenses their expression. Together these five form a T-helper-subset specification module.
role_in_a: In breast cancer this module would operate in tumor-infiltrating CD4+ T cells, setting the Th1/Th2/Th17/Treg composition of the immune infiltrate that shapes anti-tumor immunity and response to immunotherapy; GATA3 additionally acts outside the immune compartment as the master transcription factor of luminal mammary epithelial differentiation, the role its cited breast-cancer papers (growth/metastasis suppression, endocrine resistance) actually describe.
role_in_b: In psoriasis, RORC-driven Th17 cells producing IL17A, IL17F, IL22 and expressing IL23R/CCR6 are the established central effector population of the disease (the basis for IL-17/IL-23-pathway biologics); GATA3 is reported here specifically as reduced in psoriatic epidermis and restored by phototherapy, an epidermal-differentiation role distinct from its T-cell Th2 function; HLX, MSC and TCF12 would set the Th1/Treg/Th17 balance of the dermal and epidermal T-cell infiltrate alongside RORC.
shared_axis: Both tissues carry a CD4+ T-cell infiltrate whose helper-subset identity is set by this same small transcription-factor set (GATA3/RORC/HLX/MSC downstream of TCF12); which subset the network favors in each tissue would determine whether the outcome is tumor immune evasion/promotion in breast cancer or Th17-driven chronic inflammation in psoriasis, rather than the diseases sharing one fixed direction of effect.
reasoning: The module is nameable from well-established immunology (GATA3/RORC/HLX as the classical Th2/Th17/Th1 master regulators, TCF12 as their upstream E-protein) and GATA3 is independently placed by retrieved literature in both diseases. But the retrieved record only weakly carries the rest: no paper here documents RORC, HLX, MSC or TCF12 in psoriasis, and the two psoriasis papers surfaced alongside RORC (on IRF4 and adenylyl cyclase) do not discuss RORC itself. The disease-connecting claim therefore rests on general Th-subset biology rather than on anything retrieved for this specific pair, which keeps this at 'supported' rather than 'established' and at moderate rather than strong strength.
support: PMID 42520932 (GATA3 suppresses growth/metastasis in luminal breast cancer), PMID 41866545 (GATA3 in a CXCL12/ZNF503/MMP1 axis in triple-negative breast cancer), PMID 41995771 (GATA3-RFPL3-ASK1 axis suppresses breast cancer growth/metastasis), PMID 21611195 (GATA3 decreased in psoriatic epidermis, induced by phototherapy), PMID 42552187 (TCF12 expression assessed in early invasive breast cancer). No retrieved PMID places RORC, HLX or MSC (the transcription factor) directly in either disease; the MSC-tagged psoriasis and breast-cancer papers (41571652, 41007656, 36925706, 42169152, 42522822) describe mesenchymal stromal/stem cells, a distinct entity from the MSC/musculin transcription factor, and are not used as evidence here.
how_to_falsify: Sort CD4+ T cells from breast tumor infiltrates and from lesional psoriatic skin, and by CUT&RUN/ChIP test whether GATA3, RORC, HLX and MSC co-occupy the canonical Th-lineage loci (IL4/IL13, IL17A/IL22/IL23R, IFNG, FOXP3) in both cell populations, with TCF12 binding required for their accessibility at the pro-T stage; if these factors do not co-occupy the same lineage loci in both tissues' infiltrates, the shared-module account is wrong. A cheaper first test: check whether RORC (Th17) expression or activity in breast tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes tracks with GATA3 activity the way it does across the psoriasis patient groups here — a null result would undercut the claim that the two diseases share this specific balance.
caveats: Breast (epithelial/stromal) vs skin (epidermal/dermal) tissue pairing means this module, if real, is operating in the shared immune-infiltrate compartment rather than in the resident cells of either organ — except for GATA3, whose retrieved evidence is actually about epithelial/epidermal differentiation, not T cells, in both tissues. Support fractions for the five carrying factors run 94–115 of 312 patient-group comparisons (about 30–37%), a real but modest majority, not near-universal concordance; TCF4, ETS1 and MEF2C, which also touch immune or lineage biology, were left out of the carrying set because they are discordant, suggesting the module runs in different directions between the two diseases rather than uniformly the same one. Open Targets records no psoriasis association for RORC despite its established mechanistic role, a reminder that a functional Th17 master regulator need not show up as a disease-association hit. The single-view exclusions (FOS, CTNNB1, GFI1B, VDR, etc.) and tissue-generic exclusions removed likely pan-tissue or one-off signals, so their absence here is expected and not counter-evidence.
